To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found that TDP-43 is mislocalized in oligodendocytes in active lesions in MS and that there is nuclear depletion of TPD-43 in oligdendrocytes and PTB2 in neuronal cells in MS.

we identified mislocalized TDP43 and PTB in MS lesions and nuclear depletion of TPD43 in oligodentrocytes under low nutrient conditions, suggesting that altered RNA-binding proteins may contribute to the demyelination in MS.

we found mislocalized TDP43, decreased PTB1, decreased nuclear expression of neuronal PTB2, and nuclear depletion of TPD43 in human MS lesions and in human brain–derived primary oligodendroglial cells in culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathogenesis of MS and its relationship to ALS.
RNA-binding proteins and their role in demyelination in MS.
the role of RNA-binding proteins in MS pathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results are suggestive of altered expression and mis-localization of these RNA binding proteins in MS lesions.
there is evidence that TDP-43 may be involved in the pathogenesis of MS, but the evidence is not conclusive.

there is evidence of nuclear depletion of Tdp-43 in oligdendrocytes and of mislocalization of PTB in neurons in MS lesions, but there is no evidence of nuclear depletion or mislocalization of FUS in MS lesions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the altered expression and mis-localization of RBPs may play an important role in the pathogenesis of MS and may be a therapeutic target.

the RNA-binding protein (RBP) transactivation response (TAR)-DNA–binding protein of 43-kDa (TDP43), fused in sarc (FUS), polypyrimidine-tract–binding protein ( PTB) are mislocalised in MS lesions, and that the mislocalisation of TDP43 is induced by low nutrient stress.
TDP-43 and PTB are involved in the pathogenesis of oligodendroglial and neuronal degeneration in MS.

we found mislocalization of the RNA binding protein, TDP43 in MS lesions and in cultured oligodendroglia.
